problem: RL agents (A2C/A3C with CNNs) fail to learn policies in sparse-reward navigation and need extra intrinsic-reward modules (ICM, D-ACM) that add parameters and training cost.
motivation: Real-world navigation has rare external rewards, so policies are hard to learn. CapsNets preserve spatial relationships between features, which may give better state embeddings for exploration without curiosity rewards.
key_idea: Pair a compact Capsule Network (one conv layer, primary and dense capsules with dynamic routing, LSTM) with A2C, using only extrinsic reward, to navigate sparse-reward ViZDoom mazes.
insight: A CNN-only A2C without intrinsic reward failed in all scenarios, while the capsule version converged in dense ones. Adding intrinsic reward to Caps-EM (Caps-EM (IR), Table 3) made convergence 35-78% slower, though it helped a bit in the extremely sparse mirrored scenarios. Curriculum learning from MWH to MWH-M lets Caps-EM converge in the sparse mirrored settings where it otherwise fails within 1e8 steps.
method: Input/encoder: 42x42 RGB frame through a single 3x3 conv + BN + ELU (more convs were found to hurt the capsules)
Primary Capsule layer: 9x9 conv stride 2, 32 channels, capsule dim 8, Squash activation
Dense Capsule layer: 196 input capsules (dim 8) routed to 4 output capsules (dim 16) with 3 dynamic-routing iterations
Policy/value heads: LSTM plus linear layers give the policy pi and the value V; trained with A2C (synchronous) using extrinsic reward only
Curriculum learning: pretrain on MWH, then load weights to train on MWH-M
Regularization: early stopping; dropout tested (0.25 and 0.5) without significant benefit

setting.backbone: Capsule network (conv + primary/dense capsules + LSTM) with A2C, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: RL online interaction in ViZDoom My Way Home scenarios (up to ~1e8 steps); no extra data
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward, move left, move right, no action

numbers_note: Not a standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmark; results are convergence times and parameter counts in ViZDoom My Way Home, mostly in Tables 1-5 and figures. Convergence times (seconds) and params are given in the results text.
results: Caps-EM has 515,301 params (44% fewer than ICM, 83% fewer than D-ACM by the paper's figure) and 6.2 ms per training step vs 13.6 ms for ICM. Averaged over the four MWH variants it converges 1141% faster than ICM and 437% faster than D-ACM, e.g. 1.24E+4 s vs 1.46E+5 s for ICM on Dense Varied. It is worse on MWH Sparse Varied (1.07E+5 s vs 5.44E+4 s for ICM), fails on MWH-M sparse without curriculum, and no method converges on MWH-G sparse.
limitations: Fails or is slow in extremely sparse scenarios (MWH-M Sparse Uniform/Varied without curriculum; MWH-G sparse for all methods)
Capsule layers tend to overfit, needing early stopping; evaluated only on static ViZDoom mazes with RGB input, no real robots or standard navigation benchmarks
